method_limits: arm B classifies a reader by its source text (ufeff / utf-8-sig / ast.parse), not by running it
exposure is measurable only for a study that exposes a zero-argument corpus(); a study whose corpus needs arguments is published as unexposed, never as safe
the replay runs the study's own build() once per arm in a subprocess with REPLAY_TIMEOUT=900s; a timeout or a non-dict payload is payload_unavailable
every write during a replay is backed up before the open and restored after, and each restoration is published per file (E493 family)
the structural diff reports dotted paths, so a re-ordered list of equal elements reads as a change; the diff is capped at 40 rows
arm A publishes both the canonical scan (E491/E492/E495) and the full tree, because a per-study corpus walks more files than the canonical scan

arm_a_canonical.rule: the shared canonical source scan of E491/E492/E495 over this repo, minus this study's own sources

arm_a_full_tree.rule: every source the tree scan walks, so a per-study corpus is not under-counted by the canonical filters

arm_b_study_population.rule: every in-repo module under scripts/ that defines build(); a module without build() is outside the population and is never counted as safe

replay_budget.note: slowest arm observed 2026-11-07: e429_two_hop_writer raw 231.9s / stripped 237.0s, i.e. 99% of the previous 240s budget; the budget was raised to 900s so the reading is not set by it, and the earlier 240s reading is published beside this one
